2023_020_5e_tcc_course_catalog.paragraph: The 2023-2024 Course Description Book for Troy College and Career High School (TCCHS) sets out graduation requirements, department-by-department course offerings, online-program catalogs, and Oakland Schools Technical Campus options, carried as item 5E on the Troy School District Board of Education agenda dated September 19, 2023. Students must earn 19.5 credits for a TCCHS diploma, against the 22.5 credits required for a Troy High School or Athens High School diploma, while still completing 8 semesters/4 years of high school and the 18 credits required by the Michigan Department of Education. The school is led by Principal Mrs. Angela Milanov at 1522 East Big Beaver Road, Troy, MI 48083.

**Publication**
Course Description Book, 2023-2024, Troy College and Career High School (TCCHS), Troy School District. Dr. Richard Machesky, Superintendent of Schools. Board item 5E; meeting date September 19, 2023.

**Contacts and Addresses**
- TCCHS: Mrs. Angela Milanov, Principal; 1522 East Big Beaver Road, Troy, MI 48083; 248.823.5156
- Troy School District: 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, MI 48098-4799; (248)823-4000
- Department of Teaching & Learning: 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; 248.823.5221
- Oakland Schools Technical Campus - Southeast: 5055 Delemere Street, Royal Oak, MI (north of 14 Mile between Crooks and Coolidge); www.ostconline.com

**Nondiscrimination Policy (Revised August 2023)**
Cites Title IX of the Educational Amendments of 1972, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, and the Americans with Disabilities Act. Jordan M. Harris, J.D., Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, is named Title IX and Section 504/ADA Coordinator for employment and personnel matters; the District's Director of Special Education serves as Section 504/ADA Coordinator for handicapped and suspected handicapped students. Questions are directed to John Pagel, Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, Title IX and Section 504/ADA Coordinator.

**Credit Rules**
TCCHS students need 19.5 credits for a Troy School District diploma; a Troy High School or Athens High School diploma requires 22.5 credits. All TCCHS students must complete 8 semesters/4 years of high school and the 18 credits required by the Michigan Department of Education. Students with demonstrated need may request a counselor or administrator meeting to deviate from the 19.5-credit requirement. Flexibility options, updated 9.2015 under MCL 380.1278a and MCL 380.1278b, include Personal Curriculum, physical education credit through athletics or approved activities, world-language substitutions, and CTE program completion exchanged 1:1 for science, world language, or Algebra 2 requirements.

**Graduation Requirements, Beginning with the Class of 2023**

| Area | Credits | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| English | 4.0 | Literature, Informational Reading and Writing, Communications, other English electives |
| Science | 3.0 | Biology 1.0, Chemistry 0.5, Physics 0.5, Science Elective 1.0 |
| Mathematics | 4.0 | Algebra 1 1.0, Geometry 1.0, Algebra 2 1.0, math elective or math-related in final year |
| Social Studies | 3.0 | World History/Geography 1.0, American History/Geography 1.0, Economics 0.5, Government and Civics 0.5 |
| Physical Education/Health | 1.0 | Physical Education 0.5, Health 0.5 |
| World Language | 2.0 | 2.0 world language, or 1.0 world language plus 1.0 CTE or 1.0 VPAA |
| Visual, Performing, Applied Arts & Electives | 2.0 | 1.0 VPAA, 1.0 elective |
| TCCHS Program Requirements | 0.5 | Careers |
| Online Learning Experience | 0.0 | Non-credit requirement embedded in Troy classes |
| State Assessments | 0.0 | Michigan required assessments during high school |
| **Total** | **19.5** | |

**Departments**
Career Technical Education (Woodworking Design & Fabrication 1, 2, 3); English (Literature, Informational Reading and Writing, Communications, Creative Writing 1 and 2, Film and Literature, Literature of Suspense, Short Stories, Music Literature, Science Fiction); Fine Arts (Drawing 1, Advanced Drawing, Painting 1, Advanced Painting, Studio Art, Applied Arts and Design, Computer Graphics 1, Principles of Photography 1, Intro to Music Technology and Recording); Health; Mathematics (Business Math in Algebra A/B, Geometry by Design, Personal Finance/Financial Well-Being, Algebra 1, Geometry, Financial Management, School-Based Enterprise); Multi-Departmental (Innovation Exploration, Innovation Learning, Innovation Lab, Work Based Learning); Physical Education; Science (Introductory Biology, Active Chemistry/Earth Science, Chemistry 1, Organic Chemistry, Introductory Physics, Physics 1, Forensic Science, Environmental Science, Human Impact on the Earth A/B); Social Studies (AP Art History, World History/Geography 1 and 2, American History/Geography 1 and 2, Economics, Government and Civics); World Language (Spanish 1, 2, 3, 4 and Spanish AP).

**Online and Technical Options**
The Inspire Online Program runs on the Edgenuity platform; the Intersect Online Program runs through the Pearson Connexus platform. Health, Intro to Physical Activity (Level 1), and the full Spanish sequence are delivered through Edgenuity. OSTC-SE recommends generally 1.5 credits per semester; morning classes begin 7:50 AM and dismiss 10:20 AM, afternoon classes begin 12:00PM and dismiss 2:30 PM. OSTC credits are not NCAA approved.

**Grievance Procedure**
Written grievances go to the Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services within 10 workdays of the incident, with meetings and written answers at fixed intervals across three steps ending with the Superintendent, whose decision is final and binding.
2023_020_5e_tcc_course_catalog.verbose:
Course Description Book for 2023-2024, Troy College and Career High School (TCCHS), Troy School District, presented as board item 5E with a meeting date of September 19, 2023. The cover identifies Dr. Richard Machesky as Superintendent of Schools. The catalog opens with the district's Policy of Nondiscrimination, revised August 2023, then moves through credit rules, department course descriptions, online program course lists, Oakland Schools Technical Campus offerings, the antidiscrimination grievance procedure, and a graduation-requirement chart effective beginning with the Class of 2023.

**Nondiscrimination policy and coordinators.** The notice addressed to students, parents, and citizens of the Troy School District cites Title IX of the Educational Amendments of 1972, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, and the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). Troy School District states it does not discriminate on the basis of sex or handicap in admission or access to, treatment or employment in, its programs and activities, and that it periodically reviews educational and employment programs for Title IX and Section 504/ADA compliance. A grievance procedure is available through any school office or the coordinator; a School District employee in a bargaining unit may instead use the grievance procedure in the collective bargaining agreement. In accordance with Federal regulations, the district has appointed Jordan M. Harris, J.D., Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, as Title IX and Section 504/ADA Coordinator for employment and personnel matters, and the District's Director of Special Education as Section 504/ADA Coordinator for handicapped and suspected handicapped students. Questions, suggestions, or concerns are directed to John Pagel, Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, Title IX and Section 504/ADA Coordinator, Troy School District, 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, MI 48098-4799, (248)823-4000.

**School identification.** Troy College and Career High School is led by Mrs. Angela Milanov, Principal, at 1522 East Big Beaver Road, Troy, MI 48083, telephone 248.823.5156. A later page lists the Department of Teaching & Learning at 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.5221.

**Credit requirements and flexibility.** All students attending TCCHS must earn 19.5 credits to be eligible for a Troy School District high school diploma. Students seeking a diploma from Troy High School or Athens High School must meet the credit requirements in the THS and AHS course description book, totaling 22.5 credits. In alignment with the needs of alternative education students, TCCHS permits students with demonstrated need to deviate from the 19.5-credit requirement; any TCCHS student may request a meeting with a counselor or administrator about that option. All enrolled students must complete 8 semesters/4 years of high school and the 18 credits required by the Michigan Department of Education. Graduation Requirement Flexibility Options, updated 9.2015 under MCL 380.1278a and MCL 380.1278b, comprise: Personal Curriculum, allowing additional credits in some core academic areas in lieu of requirements in others; Physical Education Credit earned through athletics, extra-curricular activities, or a counselor-approved PE class; a World Language Requirement of 2.0 credits with flexibility for non-English heritage language proficiency, international study and residence, and substitution of Career & Technical Education or Visual & Performing or Applied Arts credits; and Career & Technical Education (CTE) Program Completion, whose credits may be exchanged on a 1:1 basis for required science or world language credits, or satisfy the Algebra 2 requirement when Algebra 2 content is embedded.

**Career Technical Education.** Woodworking Design & Fabrication 1, 2, and 3 each carry 1/2 credit per semester and each satisfies 1 credit of the math-related graduation requirement during the 12th grade year. Level 1 has no prerequisite and introduces designing, drawing, and manufacturing using CAD software, hand and power tools, power machines, and automation (CNC and 3D printing). Level 2 requires Woodworking Design 1 and emphasizes CAD design, CNC design and production, and advanced furniture and cabinet making. Level 3 requires Woodworking Design 2 and continues the curriculum with heavy industry influence.

**English Department.** Literature carries 1/2 credit per semester with 4 semesters required (2.0 credits total) and uses a competency-based skill framework across short stories, poetry, and novels, covering American literary eras, world literature, and forms of prose and verse. Informational Reading and Writing carries 1/2 credit per semester with 2 semesters required (1.0 credit total) and focuses on non-fiction, data mining, note taking, synthesis, summarizing, research, and position writing. Communications carries 1/2 credit per semester with 1 semester required and covers non-verbal, verbal, visual, written, and communal styles, elements of journalism, debate, and public speaking. Electives at 1 semester and 1/2 credit each include Creative Writing 1 (grades 10-12), Creative Writing 2 (prerequisite Creative Writing 1), Film and Literature, Literature of Suspense (authors named include Edgar Allan Poe, Mary Shelley, and Stephen King), Short Stories, Music Literature, and Science Fiction. Several electives require successful completion of freshmen year English. The Music Literature entry also carries text describing fundamental Pro Tools recording software concepts, original musical pieces, multi-track live audio, MIDI sequences, and virtual instruments.

**Fine Arts Department.** Offerings at 1 semester and 1/2 credit include Drawing 1; Advanced Drawing (prerequisite Drawing 1, with color as a focus); Painting 1 (water-soluble media); Advanced Painting (prerequisite Painting 1); Studio Art, with portfolio preparation as the goal and possible scheduling during Advanced Placement Art; Applied Arts and Design; Computer Graphics 1, teaching Photoshop alongside art history and theory; Principles of Photography 1, covering framing, composition, rule of thirds, light, texture, pattern lines, symmetry, depth of field, distance, perspective, culture, space, balance, color, and black and white photography; and Intro to Music Technology and Recording, using state-of-the-art studio gear and ProTools.

**Health Department.** Health is 1 semester, 1/2 credit, and is required for graduation. Topics include healthy lifestyles, violence, sexual harassment, nutrition, fitness and weight control (including steroids and eating disorders), alcohol and drug abuse, tobacco, human sexuality, birth control, and sexually transmitted diseases including HIV/AIDS. The course is taken online through the Edgenuity platform.

**Mathematics Department.** Business Math in Algebra A/B (Algebra 1 students) / Business Math A/B (Algebra 2 students) runs 4 semesters at 1/2 credit per semester; students operate an advanced fabrication lab business customizing textile products and manufacturing items of wood, metal, and/or plastic, with proceeds self-funding the venture and supporting community service or monetary gifts to local charities, and skill sets in sublimation, CNC operations, rapid prototyping, composite technologies, alternative energies, and automation robotics. Geometry by Design runs 2 semesters at 1/2 credit per semester and integrates geometry with building and construction trades. Personal Finance/Financial Well-Being runs 2 semesters at 1/2 credit per semester and is based on Michigan Personal Finance Competencies. Algebra 1 and Geometry each run 2 semesters at 1/2 credit per semester, with Algebra 1 a prerequisite for Geometry. Financial Management is 1 semester, 1/2 credit, satisfies 1/2 credit of the math-related graduation requirement, and includes a stock market game simulation and a budget challenge. School-Based Enterprise runs 2 semesters at 1/2 credit per semester, satisfies 1 credit of the math-related graduation requirement during the 12th grade year, and has students manage and operate a school store.

**Multi-Departmental.** Innovation Exploration (1 semester, 1/2 credit per semester) covers career research, resume writing, job applications, interviewing, mentors in trades and professional fields, a career portfolio, and an online educational plan. Innovation Learning (1 semester, 1/2 credit per semester) and Innovation Lab (prerequisite Innovation Learning 1, 1/2 credit) reference creatinginnovators.com and http://dschool.stanford.edu/, influenced by the "D school" at Stanford University, with the second semester devoted to a personal innovative project. Work Based Learning requires the student to hold a job and work at least 8 hours weekly; the teacher visits the student at work and creates goals with the supervisor. The catalog notes that not all listed courses are offered each year.

**Physical Education Department.** Intro to Physical Activity (Level 1) is 1 semester, 1/2 credit, taken online through the Edgenuity platform.

**Science Department.** Introductory Biology (2 semesters, 1/2 credit per semester); Active Chemistry/Earth Science (2 semesters, 1/2 credit per semester); Chemistry 1 (2 semesters, 1/2 credit per semester, prerequisite Algebra 1, satisfies 1 credit of the math-related graduation requirement during the 12th grade year); Organic Chemistry (1 semester, 1/2 credit, prerequisite Chemistry 1, with lab experiences including melting point determination, distillation, and fermentation); Introductory Physics (2 semesters, 1/2 credit per semester, prerequisites Introductory Biology and Algebra 1, satisfies 1 credit of the math-related requirement in 12th grade, aligned to the Michigan High School Content Standards and Expectations and fulfilling the state one-year chemistry-or-physics requirement); Physics 1 (2 semesters, 1/2 credit per semester, satisfies 1 credit of the math-related requirement in 12th grade, with Geometry completion and Algebra 2 enrollment highly recommended); Forensic Science (1 semester, 1/2 credit); Environmental Science (1 semester, 1/2 credit); and Human Impact on the Earth A/B (2 semesters, 1/2 credit per semester).

**Social Studies Department.** Advanced Placement Art History (2 semesters, 1/2 credits per semester); World History/Geography 1 (1 semester, 1/2 credit), beginning with the collapse of Rome and ending with the French Revolution and defeat of Napoleon; American History/Geography 1 and 2, a 1-year course divided into 2 semesters at 1/2 credit per semester covering United States development from 1877; Economics (1 semester, 1/2 credit); Government and Civics (1 semester, 1/2 credit); and World History/Geography 2 (1 semester, 1/2 credit), beginning with the Industrial Revolution and ending with current issues.

**World Language Department.** Spanish 1 through Spanish 4 each run 2 semesters at 1/2 credit per semester with sequential prerequisites, and Spanish AP (2 semesters, 1/2 credit per semester, prerequisite Spanish 4) follows College Board AP Spanish Language and Culture guidelines. Spanish 1 targets Novice-mid to Novice-high on the ACTFL Proficiency Guidelines. All Spanish courses are completed on the online Edgenuity platform.

**Online programs.** Two high school course lists are included: the Inspire Online Program, with classes on the Edgenuity platform, and the Intersect Online Program, with classes through the Pearson Connexus platform. The appended course list names offerings including Advertising and Sales Promotion; African American Studies (Black History); Algebra 1 A/B; Algebra 2 A Part 1&2; Algebra 2 A/B; Algebra 2B Part 1&2; Algebra with Finance A/B; Animation 1A/B; AP Biology A/B; AP Calculus ABA/B; AP English Language & Composition A/B; AP English Literature & Composition A/B; AP Environmental Science A/B; AP Human Geography A/B; AP Macroeconomics; AP Microeconomics; AP Psychology; AP Spanish A/B; AP Statistics A/B; AP U.S. Government and Politics; AP U.S. History A/B; Art History A/B; Art in World Cultures A/B; Astronomy A/B; Biology A/B; Business Applications; Calculus A/B; Chemistry A/B or Physics A/B; Coding 1 A/B; Consumer Math A/B; Current Events; Digital Photography 1 A/B and 2; Earth Science A/B (Honors Available); Economics; English 9, 10, 11, and 12 A/B; Entrepreneurship A/B; Environmental Science A/B; Explorations in Math A/B; French 1, 2, 3, & 4 A/B; Fundamentals of English Composition; Game Design A/B; Game Design for Chromebooks A/B; Geography and Society; Geometry A/B; German 1, 2, & 3 A/B; Gothic Literature; Government; Health; Health, Fitness, and Nutrition A/B; History of the Holocaust; Human Geography; International Business; Introduction to Drawing; Introduction to Grammar and Composition; Introduction to Graphic Design A/B; Living Music I & II; Marine Science A/B; Music Appreciation; Mythology and Folklore; Nutrition and Wellness; Personal Fitness; Personal Health and Safety with Sex Education; Physical Education, Physical Education II A/B, and Physical Education III A/B; Physical Science A/B (Honors Available); Pre-Calculus A/B (Honors Available); Principles of Business & Finance A/B; Principles of Marketing A/B; Psychology A/B; Sociology 1&2; Spanish 1, 2, 3, & 4 A/B; Statistics; U.S. History A/B; World Geography; and World History A/B.

**Oakland Schools Technical Campus.** OSTC-SE is described as an extension of the home high school, with students attending high school half the day and the technical campus the other half. Programs are organized in clusters staffed by instructors holding both a Michigan Teaching Certificate and Vocational Authorization. Several programs qualify students for advanced standing or college credit; students may attend one or two years, with the second year providing advanced work, specialization, and a certificate of completion. Programs are offered to juniors and seniors on a selective basis; OSTC recommends high school credit based on local district requirements, generally 1.5 credits per semester. If regular students carry six (6) credits, OSTC students must carry three (3) credits at their home high school in addition to three (3) credits at OSTC. Two sessions operate: Morning Session classes begin 7:50 AM and are dismissed 10:20 AM; Afternoon Session classes begin 12:00PM and are dismissed 2:30 PM. Sophomores and juniors may apply for the following year, with an exploration tour in the Fall and online application at www.ostconline.com by the end of February. The Southeast Campus is at 5055 Delemere Street, Royal Oak, MI, north of 14 Mile between Crooks and Coolidge, grades 11-12, with codes 08101 Session 1 AM and 08102 Session 2 PM. Programs listed: Automotive Technology (must begin in 11th grade), Collison Repair and Refinishing, Computer Programming, Computer Networking, Construction Technology, Culinary Arts / Hospitality, Electrical and Energy Technologies, Entrepreneurship & Advanced Marketing, Health Sciences, Machining, Mechatronics, Visual Imaging Technology, Welding, and Homeland Security (Criminal Justice or Cyber Security). The Northeast Campus in Pontiac, MI offers Cosmetology, which must begin in 11th grade. Credits offered at OSTC are not NCAA approved. A bus transports students to OSTC-SE and back; afternoon session students must provide their own transportation home from OSTC-SE or the high schools, and students who drive or ride with another assume all related responsibilities.

**Antidiscrimination grievance procedure.** Any student or employee who believes he or she has been discriminated against, denied a benefit, or excluded from participation based on sex (including sexual harassment), race, color, religion, national origin, age (employees only), height, weight, marital status, or handicap files a written grievance with the Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, the designated compliance administrator; forms are available in the Employee Services Department. Step 1 requires a written grievance form to the immediate supervisor or administrator within 10 workdays of the incident; not later than the next workday the administrator sends a copy to the Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services; within 5 workdays of the filing date the supervisor meets the grievant; within 3 workdays of that meeting a written answer is given. Step 2: within 3 workdays of receiving the answer the grievant may appeal to the Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services; within 10 workdays of the appeal the Assistant Superintendent (or Deputy Superintendent, if appropriate) meets the grievant; within 5 workdays of the meeting a written answer is given. Step 3: within 3 workdays of receiving that answer the grievant may appeal to the Superintendent; within 10 workdays the Superintendent meets the grievant; within 5 workdays the Superintendent gives a written answer, which is final and binding on all parties. The Superintendent, Deputy Superintendent, and Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services may designate representatives. A grievance not filed or appealed within the time limits is conclusively deemed abandoned; failure of an administrator to hold a meeting or render a decision allows automatic appeal to the next level; time limits may be extended only by mutual written agreement. Records are treated confidentially, and no record is kept in a staff member's personnel file if the final decision is that there was no reasonable basis for the grievance.

**Graduation requirements beginning with the Class of 2023.** English 4.0 credits, including Literature, Informational Reading and Writing, Communications, and other English electives. Science 3.0 credits: Biology 1.0, Chemistry 0.5, Physics 0.5, Science Elective 1.0. Mathematics 4.0 credits: Algebra 1 1.0, Geometry 1.0, Algebra 2 1.0 (which may be met through CTE program completion, e.g., OSTC), plus a math elective or math-related course during the final year of high school. Social Studies 3.0 credits: World History/Geography 1.0, American History/Geography 1.0, Economics 0.5, Government and Civics 0.5. Physical Education/Health 1.0 credit: Physical Education 0.5 (which may be earned through approved extracurricular athletics or activities) and Health 0.5. World Language 2.0 credits, met either as 2.0 credits of world languages or 1.0 credit of world language plus either 1.0 credit of Career Technical Education or 1.0 credit of Visual, Performing, or Applied Arts. Visual, Performing, Applied Arts & Electives 2.0 credits: 1.0 credit VPAA and 1.0 credit elective. TCCHS Program Requirements 0.5 credit in Careers. Online Learning Experience 0.0, a non-credit requirement embedded in Troy classroom experiences throughout middle and high school. State Assessments 0.0, requiring completion of the State of Michigan required assessments as administered during high school. Total Credits 19.5, the amount students are required to earn to graduate from Troy College and Career High School.
